## Summary

I implemented the dual trigger representation in `SummarizationMiddleware` at `libs/langchain_v1/langchain/agents/middleware/summarization.py`. The class already existed with a single `_trigger_conditions` attribute holding normalized dicts; I split it into the two representations the task requires:

- **`_trigger_clauses`** — the canonical list of trigger dicts (including compound multi-key clauses), produced by the existing `_normalize_trigger`, which already converts tuples like `('messages', 5)` to `{'messages': 5}` and wraps a single dict input in a list.
- **`_trigger_conditions`** — the legacy view: a list of `(key, value)` tuples derived only from single-key clauses, with compound clauses excluded.

I also repointed the two internal consumers (the `requires_profile` check and `_should_summarize`, which both need the full compound-aware clause list) from `_trigger_conditions` to `_trigger_clauses`, preserving existing runtime behavior. No test files were modified.
